what_happened: Job 20261114-160745-8e6x (code job: record the pre-verdict criteria self-check on every producer attempt) failed in planning in round 1 of 5, before any code was written. The critic judged that the accepted reading misread the request. The request said the failing stage, introspection, should get the missing information through its brief, its system facts or its inputs. The reading instead treated the "stored event" as the producer invocation record. It also claimed that a passing check leaves no stored event. That claim is false, because the passing report's criteria_check is already stored in candidate.producer_report. The real gap is that introspection's event, built in event_of_job from the outcome reason and verification details, never includes that data. The plan copied the reading's error: it wrote the self-check to the producer's invocation detail, which neither introspection nor the verifier reads. The critic gave three major findings (the fix is stored where the reporting stage never looks, the "no stored record" claim is false, and the tests only show the producer record gained a string). It also gave two minor findings and one nit. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The reading was accepted without tracing the request's phrases ("stored event", "inputs its reader receives") to the code that defines them. The stored event is the introspection Event built in event_of_job, not the producer invocation record. Nothing checks a reading's claims about what is or is not stored, or which stage consumes a record, against the code before planning starts. The plan then inherited the false premise. The same names (event, record, detail) are used for several different stored objects, so a reading can attach a request phrase to the wrong one.
other_causes: The request names the failing stage's inputs in general terms and does not give the function or file that builds the introspection event.
The plan's tests only prove the producer's own record gained a string. They do not prove the introspection reader sees it, so the plan could look complete while missing the goal.
Data flow is split: the producer report, the verifier input (D32) and the introspection event are separate stores. Nothing documents which stage reads which store.
open_hypotheses: The 5-round planning budget may let the critic's correction be absorbed in round 2. The event does not show why the job ended failed at round 1 of 5 and not after later rounds.
The reading may have been shaped by an earlier failed job's wording. The given fields do not show it.
contradictions: The event says planning stopped at round 1 of 5, yet the job ended failed. The critic's findings are fixable (keep the producer change and add the data to the event), so this does not look like a planning failure that needed to end the job.
The five earlier cases in class bn5c are planner deadline failures with no critic findings. This event has specific critic findings, so it does not fit that class.
prevention: Before a reading is accepted, check by code that each stored-data claim in it resolves. Each named record or event must map to a concrete builder function and its reader, and each "X is not stored" claim must be checked against the record types. The reading must name the consuming stage and the file where its input is built. Reject or return the reading when the consumer of the changed data is not the stage the request names. Planning demonstrations should also be required to show the consuming stage's input, not only the writer's record.
proposed_request: Make introspection see the producer's pre-verdict criteria self-check. In `event_of_job` (crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs), add the per-criterion status and evidence from `candidate.producer_report.criteria_check` to the event for a job rejected on an unmet criterion, so the event's `what` shows how each criterion stood before the final verdict. Do not claim that a passing self-check leaves no stored record, because it is already kept in `candidate.producer_report`. Writing the self-check to the producer's invocation `detail` is optional. If you do it, do not overwrite detail the driver already set, and keep the existing `; redacted report: ` parse working. Acceptance: (1) a test builds an introspection event for a job rejected on an unmet criterion and asserts that the criterion's pre-verdict status appears in the event; (2) the test fails on the current tree and passes with the change; (3) existing introspect and run_pin tests still pass; (4) add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
